approved_new_question_object.question: Bringer uses Spirits May Yet Dream to turn an unearned Fear Card in the Fear deck face-up. Does turning it face-up immediately earn that card or let players resolve its Fear effect now, or must it still be earned and resolved normally?

predetermined_answer.answer: Turning it face-up only previews the card. It does not earn it or resolve its effect. The card is still earned and resolved normally, with its Fear effect waiting for the ordinary Fear resolution procedure after it is earned.
minimum_asked_facts: Turning the card face-up does not itself earn the card.
Turning it face-up does not resolve its Fear effect or grant early resolution; normal earning and resolution still apply.
no_extra_grading_requirements: No arbitrary Fear-marker count, card identity, deck depth, threshold numerical recall, or complete Fear-step recital is required.
Do not require restating current Terror rules or a victory check not asked.

approved_classification_replacements.approved_replacement_text: Q116 retains two fully graded branches. Given one simultaneous addition of two Blight to the stated land, each of the two Spirits loses one Presence there. Given two separate completed one-Blight additions, each loses Presence twice, totaling two disks per Spirit if still present. The simultaneous two-Blight producer is unverified in the assigned original core and receives zero current-base novelty credit; merely stipulating it does not verify it. simultaneous_addition.conditional_answer: One Presence per Spirit in the stated land.

two_separate_completed_additions.answer: Presence destroyed twice, two disks per Spirit if still present.

approved_classification_replacements.reasoning: The full FAQ says each time one or more Blight is added to a given land, destroy one Presence of every Spirit there. That supplies the conditional result, not the original source of a two-at-once instruction. The FAQ multi-Blight example names Sweden, which is an excluded adversary. The standard Ravage rule adds only one regardless of damage; cascades are further additions to adjacent lands. Poisoned Land plus Repeat positively supports separate additions, not simultaneity. Current core-scope-credit already maintains exactly this split, so correct the compact claim without changing that working split.

approved_question.question: An effect explicitly adds two Blight simultaneously to one land containing two Presence from each of two Spirits. Counting only Presence destroyed in that land by this one addition, how many disks does each Spirit lose? Would adding one Blight there in each of two separate completed instructions destroy Presence once or twice, assuming each Spirit still has Presence there?

approved_predetermined_answer.answer: The simultaneous addition destroys one Presence from each Spirit, even though two Blight tokens are added. Two separate additions destroy one Presence per Spirit on each addition, hence two per Spirit if available. Cascades elsewhere are outside the requested count.
